candidate.name: TraceElephant / Seeing the Whole Elephant: Understanding and Debugging Multi-Agent Systems Through Full Execution Traces

grade.generic_intermediate_checkpoint_restore_: C/not implemented as a uniform public interface located in this audit

observations.finding: The paper reports 220 annotated failed traces from 380 runs across Captain-Agent, Magentic-One and SWE-Agent, and reports that full traces improve failure localization over partial observation by up to 76.5%. It also reports a Dynamic Agentic method that replays a task trajectory to a candidate failure step, modifies the input request, and checks the next k=3 steps for correction.

The public repository includes adapted executable copies of Captain-Agent, Magentic-One and SWE-Agent plus an OpenAI-compatible logging middleware. The agent-system documentation explicitly records usability modifications: Captain-Agent search API replacement; Magentic-One Playwright-to-Patchright and Bing-to-DuckDuckGo changes. These are substantive reproducibility dependencies and mean the released environments are adapted copies, not bit-identical upstream snapshots.

Magentic-One includes a large exact-pinned requirements.txt (including autogen==0.5.3), which is strong environment evidence for that subsystem. The middleware requirements use lower-bound ranges rather than a complete exact lock. External model APIs, browser/search services and adapted upstream systems remain sources of drift.

The released code/trace_locate/inference.py exposes only all_at_once, step_by_step and binary_search. run_grid_parallel.sh invokes those same static methods and currently defaults to all_at_once. The paper's Static Agentic and Dynamic Agentic execution paths were not located in this public evaluation module. Therefore the paper's agentic localization and counterfactual headline numbers are not exact-replay-ready from the located public one-click scripts.

The released middleware.py is a transparent proxy/logger: it forwards request JSON to the upstream endpoint and logs input/output. It contains no built-in checkpoint/restore state machine or counterfactual request-replacement policy. The README explicitly invites users to modify it for dynamic functionality. Thus the paper's intervention behavior requires additional code/configuration beyond the unmodified public middleware located here.

Repository inspection did not locate a uniform generic checkpoint/restore interface across Captain-Agent, Magentic-One and SWE-Agent. This supports the clean worker's narrower statement: TraceElephant is a promising runnable substrate for a selector experiment, but standardized restoration semantics and replay-fidelity measurement still need to be implemented and validated. It does not establish a ready-made arbitrary-step long-horizon rollback harness.

The public Hugging Face dataset is distributed primarily as data.zip. Its history includes a later repair of content/tool_calls for Captain and Magentic traces, changing the archive object/size. Exact replay should therefore pin a concrete dataset revision/LFS object rather than relying on a moving main reference. This audit does not infer that the paper used the pre-repair archive; the repair predates the ACL publication.
No protocol-matched independent numerical rerun of the paper's main Static Agentic/Dynamic Agentic table was located in this audit. Mirrors/copies are not counted as independent reproduction.

dynamic_agentic_step_gain.assessment: Consistent with the paper's approximately 10% step-level improvement wording.

partial_observation_headline.assessment: The abstract's up-to-76.5% improvement is arithmetically reconstructible as degraded-to-full relative uplift. Nearby wording that calls roughly 76% and 22% an accuracy 'drop' is directionally misleading under the conventional full-to-degraded drop definition.

supported: TraceElephant publicly releases a substantial trace/debugging benchmark and adapted runnable agent-system code.
The paper reports and describes a local dynamic counterfactual procedure that replays to a candidate step, intervenes, and inspects a short next-step window.
The public artifacts make TraceElephant a plausible substrate for future controlled rollback-target experiments.
not_supported_by_this_audit: That the public repository provides a standardized arbitrary intermediate checkpoint/restore API across all three systems.
That the released one-click evaluation scripts reproduce the paper's Static Agentic or Dynamic Agentic headline results.
That local k=3 counterfactual correction proves faithful long-horizon environment restoration or global task repair.
That any paper headline has been independently reproduced under a protocol-matched third-party run.

result: B overall. The worker's core synthesis is supported and should remain narrow: TraceElephant is materially more executable than a static trace corpus, but it is not a turnkey rollback-selector testbed. Public data, adapted agent-system implementations and static localization scripts are substantial. The strongest reproducibility gap is that the located public trace_locate path implements only the three static prompting methods, while the paper's Static Agentic/Dynamic Agentic intervention path and a uniform checkpoint/restore abstraction were not located. Consequently the Dynamic Agentic 33.3-vs-30.3 step result and related intervention claims remain primary-study evidence rather than independently/publicly exact-replayed evidence. Exact future reproduction should pin both repository SHA and Hugging Face dataset revision and must separately validate restore fidelity and post-restore stochastic/control floors.
reopen_conditions: Author-affiliated publication of the exact Static Agentic and Dynamic Agentic execution code/config used for the reported tables.
A versioned arbitrary-step restore/reconstruction implementation with fidelity checks across the released agent systems.
A protocol-matched independent rerun of the main localization/counterfactual results.
A paper-linked immutable dataset revision/model API snapshot/raw output bundle sufficient to recompute the main tables.
